thread:
marta: Heads-up — I'm planning a small runbook sim tomorrow for private deployment isolation telemetry + RBAC delta. Want to validate netpols, KMS calls, and audit log fidelity before the customer dry-run.
aj: 👍 what's the scope? full cluster or just control-plane + keystore?
devon: Prefer control-plane + keystore agent + a node sim. Keep it to one AZ so we can watch egress pathing.
marta: Good call. Steps: 1) apply tightening netpols on a canary namespace 2) deploy keystore shim with debug logs 3) run synthetic decrypt/load traffic 4) verify audit entries and no unintended 403s.
kai: Add: simulate RBAC rollback (remove a serviceaccount role) to see graceful failure and alerting. We should also run a KMS latency spike (throttle) to exercise fallbacks.
aj: For netpols I can push a strict policy that only allows kubelet+keystore agent -> kms-proxy egress on port 443, and block all other egress. Example snippet I'll use:```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-egress-only
  namespace: canary-sec
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: kms-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
marta: Nice. For audit logging: we want to confirm three things — (a) KMS Decrypt/Encrypt requests are logged with trace IDs, (b) RBAC authz failures include the actor and resource path, (c) logs are forwarded to our airgapped sink.
devon: I'll add a short python harness that hits the keystore shim with a few keys, including malformed token to trigger 401/403. snippet:```python
import requests
for i in range(5):
    r = requests.post('http://keystore:8080/decrypt', json={'kid':'test-'+str(i)})
    print(r.status_code, r.text)
```
kai: Ops-bot — can you create a temporary canary commit that toggles the RBAC role binding for svcacct keystore-canary?
ops-bot: created: rbinding/keystore-canary-toggle (ttl: 2h) :white_check_mark:
aj: When we toggle RBAC, watch for noisy errors in the console; ensure we don't create a cascade that evicts pods. Add a POD disruption budget maybe.
marta: Agreed — PDB set to minAvailable:1 on keystore-agent. Also: we need to ensure audit logs include the KMS request correlation id. devon, make the harness include X-Request-ID header.
devon: will do. Also I'll capture /var/log/keystore-agent.log and the audit-forwarder output at /tmp/audit-forward.log so we can diff entries.
kai: What's our rollback plan if the netpol blocks telemetry forwarding? We should have a quick iptables accept on the node and a documented rollback k8s patch.
marta: Rollback: kubectl -n kube-system patch networkpolicy keystore-egress-only --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/egress"}]' and then restart audit-forwarder daemonset. I'll paste that into the runbook.
aj: Also watch for KMS 403 errors mapping to service account not namespace mismatch — we had that on EU-onprem last quarter. Might be a KMS key policy issue, not just RBAC.
kai: Good call. Confirm KMS principal mapping in keystore shim logs: should be "principal=svcacct:keystore-canary@namespace=canary-sec". If not, abort and revert RBAC.
ops-bot: runbook checklist created: tasks=[apply-netpol, deploy-keystore-shim(debug), run-synth-traffic, toggle-rbac, capture-logs, validate-audit-entries, rollback-if-blocked] owner=marta window=tomorrow-09:30-10:30
marta: Last ask — set alerting: if >5 audit-forwarder delivery failures in 5m OR any keystore-agent pod OOMKilled during sim, auto-rollback netpol and escalate to #eng-oncall.
devon: I'll instrument the harness to emit span IDs that correlate with audit entries, so we can grep quickly.
aj: Sounds solid. I'll be on standby. If anyone wants to review the runbook before we go live, ping me in thread.
kai: I'll add a quick netstat check to the preflight: `kubectl exec -n canary-sec $(kubectl get pods -l app=keystore-agent -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- netstat -tnp | grep 443`
marta: Perfect. Thanks all — I'll drop the runbook link when it's up. :memo:
